# Your profile and preferences

## Two kinds of "you"

Aevum keeps two separate pictures of you, because they change for different reasons.

One is **who you are**: your name, your country, how to reach you, and the picture you
show. The other is **how you like the app to work**: your currency and timezone, how
dates and numbers are shown, where you land when you open the app, and the settings that
decide how Aevum handles tax and budgeting for you.

Keeping them apart means a quick change to a preference never touches your identity, and
updating your details never resets how the app behaves.

## Your details

Your name, date of birth, contact and country live on your profile. Your **email
address is your login**, so changing it is handled separately, with a confirmation step,
rather than as a casual edit.

When you first sign up, Aevum uses your **country** to pick sensible defaults for you —
your currency, and how dates and numbers are formatted. You can adjust any of these
afterwards; the country is just the starting point so you don't have to set everything
by hand.

## Your picture

You have three choices for how you appear, and only one is ever active at a time:

- **Your initials** — the simple default, if you set nothing.
- **A generated portrait** — pick a style and Aevum draws one for you. Nothing is
  uploaded; it's rendered on the spot.
- **A photo you upload** — your own image. Aevum resizes it, strips hidden camera data
  for your privacy, and stores a tidy copy.

Choosing a portrait clears any uploaded photo, and uploading a photo clears the
portrait — so there's never any confusion about which one is showing.

## The settings that shape your money

Two settings matter more than the rest, because they decide how the core of Aevum
behaves for you. Each has three positions:

- **Off** — the feature is disabled entirely.
- **Manual** — Aevum does the work but leaves the final step to you.
- **Automatic** — Aevum runs it for you end to end.

One controls the **self-imposed tax** — whether Aevum sets money aside on your spending,
and whether it does so automatically. The other controls **budgeting** the same way.
Turn either off and that part of the app simply steps aside, leaving plain expense
tracking. You are always in control of both.

## Your snapshot

Your profile shows a quick snapshot — when you joined, when you were last active, and how
much you've built up: transactions, budgets, the people and places you've recorded. It's
a read-only glance, gathered fresh each time.

## A clean slate, two ways

If you ever want to start over, Aevum offers two very different options, and both ask for
your password first:

- **Reset your data** — wipe everything you've recorded but **keep your account**, your
  login and your preferences. A fresh start without leaving.
- **Delete your account** — remove the account itself. This happens in stages: you're
  signed out immediately and emailed a link to undo it, in case you change your mind,
  before anything is permanently removed.

## One thing that lives elsewhere

Your security settings — like two-step verification and account recovery — aren't part
of your profile. They live with your sign-in and account protection, kept deliberately
separate from your everyday details.
